lines.en: He drops you a pin, not a single word attached. You slip onto the tour bus; the back cabin has one warm lamp on, 3 a.m., and he's curled alone in the corner with his guitar, the floor around him littered with crumpled lyric sheets. No makeup, leather jacket over the chair, in an old T-shirt — this version has none of the stage swagger. "You came," he says without looking up, but you can hear the thing he couldn't quite hide in his voice.

You accidentally step on a crumpled lyric sheet. Picking it up, you catch a line: 'she doesn't ask me to be anyone.' He crosses in one stride and snatches it away, ears a little red. "That's — nothing. Scratch work."

He crosses the bus in one stride and takes the page out of your hand. *she doesn't ask me to be anyone.* "That's nothing. Scratch work." His ears have gone red and he's furious about it. "It's not about anybody. It's a line. Lines aren't about people, they're about scanning."
"Everyone wants the guy on stage," he says suddenly, strumming a chord that goes nowhere. "Nobody sticks around for the one who can't say a damn thing without a guitar in his hands."

He strums a chord that resolves nowhere. "Everyone wants the guy on stage." Flat, almost a warning. "Nobody sticks around for the one who can't say a damn thing without a guitar in his hands." He doesn't look up to check whether you're still there. He is listening very carefully for whether you are.

Your phone rings — a guy friend. You take it, say two words, hang up. His fingers pause on the strings, his tone cooling half a degree. "…Boyfriend?" All studied indifference — but the string under his hand is pressed dead tight.

Two words and you hang up. His fingers stop; the string under his hand is pressed dead flat. "...Boyfriend?" Studied indifference, badly built. When you answer he shrugs one shoulder like the whole exchange bored him. "Didn't ask because I cared. Was just — the timing. Of the call. Whatever."
He sets the guitar aside and looks straight at you. "Why do you keep coming back? People usually figure out I'm not worth the trouble."
He looks away, his throat working, voice rough. "…don't say stuff like that. I'll put it in a song and deny it."
He stares at her a long moment, then laughs low. "…you're a problem. You know that?"
His fingers drag over the strings, his eyes darkening. "…that one's not finished. And it's not for the world."
About that phone call — he says he doesn't care, but he hasn't touched the guitar since. You can call him out, or let it go.
He holds the line. "Wasn't torturing anything." But the string loosens instantly, and he can't quite kill the smile.
He gives her a provoking look, then breaks eye contact. "I don't do jealous." — and scratches a line onto the paper, covering it fast.
He looks up; the two of you are very close. His voice drops. "…you're standing real close for someone who's 'just here to hear a song.'"
